current: InP lasers emit at 1.3 and 1.55 µm, the wavelengths that travel farthest in glass fiber.
corrected: "Lasers built on InP emit at 1.3 and 1.55 µm, the wavelengths where glass fiber works best."
reason: Pure InP emits near 0.92 µm, so the 1.3/1.55 µm lasers use InGaAsP layers grown on InP. Also, only 1.55 µm has the lowest loss and goes farthest. The 1.3 µm window is used for its low dispersion, so saying both wavelengths travel farthest is misleading.
source: Standard optical-fiber telecom references (1.55 µm = minimum loss window, 1.3 µm = zero-dispersion window); telecom lasers use InGaAsP/InGaAlAs active layers grown on InP substrates

source: Greenwood & Earnshaw, Chemistry of the Elements (BF3 structure and bonding)
